key_insight: A spark plasma sintered composite with equal weight fractions of 6H-SiC and h-BN retains structural integrity under extreme oxidizing heat and exhibits nearly temperature-independent thermal conductivity.
engineering_relevance: This lightweight, machinable ceramic is a promising candidate for structural components exposed to severe heating, oxidation, and thermal cycling.
method: Spark plasma sintering of a 50:50 wt% 6H-SiC/h-BN composite.
High-velocity oxygen-fuel torch testing and surface microstructural evaluation.
Finite-element thermal analysis and ReaxFF molecular dynamics of interfacial bonding.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports survival during prolonged heating and thermal cycling at surface temperatures above 1500 °C, while pure 6H-SiC and h-BN rapidly fractured or eroded.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify exposure duration, cycle count, or retained mechanical strength, limiting assessment of service lifetime.
paper_title: SiC-BN composites with extreme thermal and environmental stability
